analysis.investment_thesis: At a P/E of 7.96 the headline multiple looks cheap, but an ROE of just 0.45% reveals that earnings are effectively trivial — the "cheap" P/E is arithmetic, not value. With a tiny INR 30.40 Cr market cap, a 2014-vintage business, and no multi-year earnings history disclosed, this fails virtually every quantitative filter I require.
key_strengths: Low headline P/E of 7.96 — superficially within the <15 threshold
High promoter holding of 69.28% — skin in the game
Asset-light IT-enabled services niche (custom learning solutions)
key_risks: ROE of 0.45% is de minimis — the business is barely profitable on equity
Micro-cap of INR 30.40 Cr with near-zero institutional ownership (FII 0.04%, DII 0%)
No disclosed multi-year earnings record, book value, current ratio, debt, or dividend — fails my data tests outright
red_flags: 0.45% ROE implies either tiny earnings on inflated equity or accounting distortion
Recently listed micro-cap — classic speculative IPO territory
No dividend history and no balance-sheet data provided — opaque to the defensive investor
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham lens, the single most important datapoint is the 0.45% ROE. A business generating under 1% return on its own equity cannot be considered to have "proven earning power" in any Graham sense — it is worse than a savings account. The P/E of 7.96 is mathematically valid but economically meaningless when the "E" is a rounding error; the apparent cheapness is an optical illusion, not a margin of safety.

I also lack the data I require to even begin a defensive analysis: no current ratio, no debt-to-equity, no book value per share, no 3–5 year EPS track record, and no dividend history. Combined with a tiny INR 30.40 Cr float, near-zero institutional ownership (FII 0.04%, DII 0.00%), and a recent-vintage listing, this sits squarely in the speculative bucket Mr. Market reserves for the unwary. Avoid.
